Working with AfriScan

How we work

Every engagement starts with your route or site and what the record is for. We reply with a written proposal: scope, imagery plan, method, deliverables and schedule. We also respond to tenders, RFQs and RFPs.

Request a proposal Send tender documents

Engagement models

Ways to work with us

Most clients start with a baseline and add re-surveys, or bring us in for one decision: a cut-off date, a route choice or a single contested location.

One-off

Baseline survey

A register of the structures within the distances you choose along a route, or inside and around a boundary, with each 500 m rated for encroachment density. The starting point for everything else.

Read

Recurring

Scheduled re-surveys

Your route or site re-surveyed on a schedule agreed with you, with an email to your team after each survey saying what has changed and where.

Read

Between dates

Change detection

New and removed structures between two or more dated surveys, flagged automatically and confirmed by a reviewer, with before-and-after views of each change.

Read

Detail where needed

Drone surveys

Orthophotos, elevation models and close checks of flagged stretches, flown by Afridrone, subject to the permits and authorisations each job requires.

Read

Project decisions

ESIA and resettlement support

Dated registers for a resettlement cut-off date, structure counts for route and site options, and estimated households for planning, for your team or your consultants.

Read

Records

Evidence packs

Dated imagery, registers and maps packaged with file fingerprints and an independent timestamp, so you can show what was on the ground and when. They support legal and community processes.

Read

Getting started

What to send us, and what you get back

What to send us

  • The route or boundary file: KML, KMZ, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GPX or GeoPackage
  • The country and province
  • The distances to report, or the zones your engineers have defined
  • The date the record must reflect, if there is one
  • The deliverables you need and your deadline
  • Any imagery you already hold

What you get back

  • A written proposal: scope, imagery plan, method, deliverables and schedule
  • The imagery options for your area, with what each can and cannot show
  • For drone work, the permits and authorisations the flight needs and how they fit the schedule
  • A named first step, often one stretch or one site, if you want to start small

For procurement teams

Tenders, RFQs and supplier forms

We respond to tenders, RFQs and RFPs. Send your supplier or prequalification forms with your request; the proposal states which registrations are in place for your contract and which are being arranged. Tell us the portal or format your process uses.

Data you send us

We never publish a client’s route, imagery or results without written permission. The only route shown on this site, a high-pressure gas pipeline in Mozambique, is shown with the route owner’s permission.

Have a tender or an RFQ?

Send the documents and the deadline; we reply in the format the tender asks for.

Send tender documents

How every project runs

The same rules on every job

Scoped in writing

Nothing is surveyed until the route, the distances, the imagery and the deliverables are agreed in the proposal.

Reviewed by a person

A person reviews every result before delivery. Uncertain structures are listed for a ground check, not guessed.

Dated and credited

Each report names its imagery and capture date where the source gives one, and credits open data as its licence requires.

Land, not people

We map structures, cleared ground, excavations and tracks. We do not track people or vehicles.

Frequently asked questions

Can we start with part of the route?

Yes. Many projects start with one stretch, one site or one concession boundary, so your team can check the register against what it knows before the rest is surveyed. Work tuned to your imagery, such as a custom detector, is tuned and checked on part of your area before it runs on the rest.

Do you respond to tenders and RFPs?

Yes. Send the tender documents or the RFQ with your request and we reply in the format the tender asks for. Send your supplier or prequalification forms too; the proposal states which registrations are in place for your contract and which are being arranged.

Can you work as part of a consultancy's team?

Yes. ESIA, RAP and engineering consultancies can commission structure registers, route comparisons and GIS layers for their own reports, delivered in the formats their teams already use.

How do you quote?

Every proposal is scoped to your route or site, the imagery it needs, the deliverables and the schedule. Send the route file and what you need to know, and the proposal will set out the whole scope in writing.

Will you publish our route or results?

No. We never publish a client’s route, imagery or results without written permission.

Ready to scope a survey or answer a tender?

Send the route or site, or the tender documents and the deadline. We reply with a scope and a written proposal in the format your process asks for.
